diagnosis_explanation:
This is a diagnosis explanation for a baby born early. The baby was born at 34 weeks gestation. This means the baby was born several weeks before the full 40 weeks. The baby is now 5 days old.

The baby was exposed to Group B Streptococcus. This is a type of bacteria. The baby did not get an infection from this exposure.

The baby has physiologic jaundice. This is a common condition in newborns. It causes yellowing of the skin and eyes. It is usually mild and goes away on its own.

The baby also has a feeding problem. This means the baby is having some trouble with eating. This could be related to being born early.
medication_rationale:
Ampicillin:
This medicine helps fight off germs that can make your baby sick. It was given to prevent an infection. You should not notice any changes. Rarely, babies may get a rash. Call your doctor if your baby gets a rash that spreads.

Gentamicin:
This medicine helps fight off germs that can make your baby sick. It was given to prevent an infection. You should not notice any changes. Rarely, babies may have trouble hearing. Call your doctor if your baby seems less responsive to sounds.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- Your baby may still need extra support breathing. This is normal.
- Your baby will be fed breast milk or formula.
- Use 20 to 24 calories per ounce for feedings.
- Watch for your baby's breathing pattern.
- Call your doctor if your baby has trouble breathing.
- Your goal is to continue successful feedings at home.

**Week 2:**
- Your baby's breathing should get more steady.
- Continue feeding breast milk or formula.
- Use 20 to 24 calories per ounce for feedings.
- Watch for signs your baby is getting enough milk.
- Call your doctor if your baby seems unwell or stops eating.
- Your goal is to have regular feeding times.

**Week 3:**
- Your baby's weight should start to increase steadily.
- Continue feeding breast milk or formula.
- Use 20 to 24 calories per ounce for feedings.
- Watch for wet diapers and bowel movements.
- Call your doctor if your baby has fewer wet diapers than usual.
- Your goal is for your baby to gain weight each day.

**Week 4:**
- Your baby should seem more alert and responsive.
- Continue feeding breast milk or formula.
- Use 20 to 24 calories per ounce for feedings.
- Watch for signs of good sleep and wake cycles.
- Call your doctor if your baby seems unusually sleepy or fussy.
- Your goal is to feed your baby on demand.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Your baby's breathing will continue to improve.
- Feeding and sleeping patterns will become more regular.
- Continue to monitor your baby closely.
- Follow up with your pediatrician as recommended.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- No symptoms in this tier for your diagnosis.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- No symptoms in this tier for your diagnosis.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Baby seems unwell: Your doctor can check your baby.
- Baby is feeding poorly: Your doctor can check feeding.
- Yellow skin or eyes: This can be jaundice.
- Baby seems sleepy: Your doctor can check if this is normal.
- Baby has trouble breathing: Your doctor can check breathing.
